about.what: Morphology package: the body of one creature as a topological entity (nodes, edges, parameters).
about.frame: x forward, y to the creature's left, z up; lengths in the generator's units (see 'size')
about.nodes: one per joint of each placed copy of a part; id = <part>[.<copy>].j<index>; index 0 is where the part starts
about.bones: one per stretch between neighbouring nodes; id = <part>[.<copy>].b<index>; 'parent' is the bone it moves with
about.edges: bone: two nodes of one chain. attach: first node of a part to a bone of its parent part, at 't' along that bone (0 = start, 1 = end). mirror: the same node on the left and right copy. radial: the same node on neighbouring copies around the parent.
about.parts: one per gene of the genome; 'copies' lists the placed copies ('' = single, L/R = mirrored, 0..N-1 = radial)
about.groups: named sets of part names, for addressing several parts at once
about.skin: per mesh vertex: up to 4 bones (indices into 'bones') and their weights (sum 1). A default binding; a motion system may ignore it and bind the mesh its own way.
about.access: read_only: a motion system may move nodes (pose) but not add, remove or rewire them. The body is grown from the genome; a change to its structure has to go back to RTIS as a gene change, and RTIS grows a new body and a new package.
about.lineage: how this body came to be. Inheritance is done by RTIS on genes; a motion system receives the result here and does not redo it. ancestry_a per part = share of the part's genes from parent A.

rules: tags: RTIS ontology.py (cell / organ / part layers)
matching: PCE layered similarity; >= 0.40 always, 0.25-0.40 chance (score - 0.25) / 0.15, < 0.25 never
each gene copied whole from one parent (alpha 0.5)
relative genes (size gene; lengths and radii as fractions; lean and bends relative to the parent)
linkage: 1 switch point per crossed part
grafting: a part whose parent is missing attaches where that parent would have been
site rule: two unmatched limbs in one place compete; only one stays
geometry: skeleton + implicit surface + Fourier cross-section detail
